verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "launch teams at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R1); "Launch Complex 39B" at Kennedy (R2); Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the launch location as Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch on Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently specify Wednesday, April 1, 2026, as the scheduled launch date.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "no earlier than 6:24 p.m. EDT, Wednesday, April 1" (R1); "Liftoff is scheduled for 6:24 p.m. EDT" (R2); "6:24 p.m." (R5, R8)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time of 6:24 p.m. EDT is directly stated in pre-launch sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch opens a two-hour window.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Liftoff is scheduled for 6:24 p.m. EDT (2224 UTC), which is the opening of a two-hour window."
verifications.reasoning: R2 explicitly states the launch opens a two-hour window.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight test around the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA’s first crewed mission under the Artemis program" (R1); "first time in more than 53 years" (R2); "first U.S. human lunar spaceflight in over 50 years" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm it as the first crewed lunar mission in 50+ years since Apollo.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is scheduled to launch from Launch Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct mentions of Launch Pad/Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center.

verifications.claim: April 2, 2026, is designated as a backup launch opportunity for Artemis II.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No source specifies April 2, 2026, as a designated backup; general backups mentioned but not this date.

verifications.claim: Broadcast coverage begins on NASA+ at 12:50 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Full launch coverage begins at 12:50 p.m. on NASA+" (R1); "Full coverage on NASA+ begins at 12:50 p.m." (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and platform directly stated.

verifications.claim: The countdown for Artemis II has already begun.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "As the Artemis II countdown moves steadily toward liftoff" (R1); "countdown officially began ticking at 4:44 p.m. EDT on Monday" (R2); "countdown clock started ticking down at 4:44 p.m. EDT" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Pre-launch sources confirm countdown has started.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "approximately 10-day journey around the Moon" (R1); "10-day mission" (R3, R4, R7, R9)
verifications.reasoning: Most sources describe it as a 10-day mission; R2 says 'more than nine-day' but consistent overall.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon and back
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "send NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen on an approximately 10-day journey around the Moon" (R1); "four astronauts will embark on an a more than nine-day mission... flying around the Moon and back" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on a mission around the Moon and back.
